title: Chat Completions compatibility: reconciliation proxy for request/response mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Redwood exposes a stable Chat/Streaming API while many customers send requests using the OpenAI Chat Completions shape (openai 'chat.completions'). Differences in streaming chunk framing, function-call semantics, and finish_reason semantics cause subtle bugs for legacy clients.

Goal: Build a lightweight reconciliation proxy that sits between the OpenAI-shaped input and Redwood's canonical request/response model. The proxy must: preserve streaming partials for low-latency consumers, preserve deterministic function/tool call envelopes, reconcile the final non-streamed response with streamed deltas, and emit reconciliation telemetry for quality monitoring.

Non-goals: Rewriting user prompts or changing model outputs, providing a full fidelity OpenAI API (we only aim for behavior parity for common patterns used by Redwood customers).

Approach: implement a two-stage proxy: 1) Stream-pass: translate OpenAI SSE chunks into Redwood internal stream frames, annotate each frame with sequence numbers and tentative offsets, and forward to runtime with minimal transformation. 2) Reconciliation-pass: when the final completion/meta packet arrives (finish_reason or final message), replay/merge streamed deltas into a canonical message payload, resolve function_call argument assembly, and emit a single final response object to the caller.

Key mapping decisions (decided during tech scoping):
- Role mapping: preserve OpenAI roles (system/user/assistant) in a "role" field but map to Redwood message IDs and content parts so downstream runtime sees our canonical schema.
- Streaming deltas: keep original delta tokens in order, attach a monotonic frame_id and earliest_token_index; do NOT attempt to token-decode in the proxy.
- Function/tool calling: treat "delta.function_call" pieces as chunked fields; accumulate "name" and "arguments" fragments, validate JSON at reconciliation time, and emit a structured "tool_invocation" object in Redwood format. If JSON parsing fails, emit a partial tool invocation with a parse_error marker and raise a quality alert.
- finish_reason handling: map OpenAI finish_reason values to Redwood reasons but preserve raw value in metadata for auditability. If final finish_reason contradicts earlier deltas (e.g., final message truncated), run merge heuristics favoring final message for non-ambiguous fields and favor streamed sequence for tokenized output.

Operational constraints: low additional latency (~<15ms median), memory bounded per session (configurable ephemeral buffer cap), robust to out-of-order SSE segments and client reconnects (idempotent reassembly key per request).

Telemetry and tracing: emit events "compat.reconcile.start", "compat.reconcile.merge_error", "compat.reconcile.success" with reasons, counts, and reconcilation latency. Hook into Console per-route dashboard for regression detection (quality-monitoring alert if >0.5% of reconciles produce parse_error).

Testing strategy: unit tests for chunk reassembly, property tests that fuzz chunk boundaries and partial JSON fragments, end-to-end test against a Redwood runtime stub and recorded OpenAI SSE traces, and manual QA with known failing customer traces (see links).

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind "compat_reconcile_v1"; gradually ramp 0 -> 100% for customers using OpenAI compatibility, monitor telemetry and rollback on regression.

Notes: design doc includes data model and telemetry schema; runtime change required to accept annotated stream frames (see dependencies).

acceptance_criteria: SSE => Redwood frame translation preserves order and attaches monotonic frame_id
Function/tool call fragments are reassembled into valid JSON for >=99.5% of recorded production traces or produce a parse_error with original fragments logged in debug mode
Reconciliation latency p50 < 15ms and p99 < 200ms under normal load (measured in canary)
Feature is behind 'compat_reconcile_v1' FF and can be toggled per-customer
Telemetry events are emitted and visible in Console dashboard; alerts fire when parse_error rate > 0.5%
